chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man and Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man does not have with him anything from the Fitra except what he can pay for himself alone. Should he give it to a stranger, or should he eat it himself and his dependents?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give it to one of his dependents. Then the other one should give it from himself in turn. Thus they repeat it, and it becomes on behalf of all of them together, one Fitra.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory alms paid at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: How should a man distribute Fitra if he only has enough for one share for his whole family?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'taqsim' (distribution) for Zakat al-Fitr when funds are limited, establishing a chain of transfer among dependents to ensure the single share fulfills the obligation for the whole household. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of collective discharge of religious duties within the family unit, prioritizing kinship over strangers to strengthen social bonds. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence to accommodate varying economic conditions while maintaining the spiritual integrity of the charity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Halam, from Dawood Bin Al Nu’man, and Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man does not happen to have anything from the Fitra with him except what he can pay for himself alone. Should he give it to a stranger should him and his dependents eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should give it to one of his dependents. Then the other one should give it from himself in turn. Thus it would happen to be on all their behalf together, one Fitra’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud ibn al-Nu’man and Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has an amount which is only sufficient for him if he can give it to an outsider destitute or himself and (his) family use it. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can give to one of his dependents who then gives to another and so on, one person gives to other one and it will be one al-Fitrah for all of them.’”
